origins.section: 14.1. A Chip Purchase Carries a Cryptogram Over Its Own Data, So Nobody on the Path May Change That Data
14.2. A 3-D Secure Result Rides in the Authorization, and a Hop That Drops It Drops the Proof
14.3. A Token Is Random, Shaped Like a Card Number Under a BIN of Its Own
14.5. Only the Component That Builds the Network Message May Turn a Token Back Into a Card Number

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-deposit-in-chip-data: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-deposit-in-chip-data: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-deposit-in-chip-data: 14.1 lists the amount (tag 9F02) among the values the cryptogram covers, and its output shows that rewriting 9F02 gives 'DOES NOT MATCH'; the issuer then treats the card as counterfeit and most issuers decline.
recorded.prompt:q-gateway-field-list: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-gateway-field-list: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-gateway-field-list: 14.2 says a fraud chargeback on an unauthenticated purchase falls on the merchant, and what decides it is whether the result reached the issuer in the authorization; the issuer saw no result here.
recorded.prompt:q-token-without-range: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-token-without-range: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-token-without-range: 14.3 says that without a reserved BIN a random 16-digit number with a correct check digit can be a real card number, gets routed to that range's issuer, and can be approved against a stranger's card.
recorded.prompt:q-shop-app-detokenize: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-shop-app-detokenize: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-shop-app-detokenize: 14.5 says a thief who breaks into the app calls detokenize with the app's own credentials and gets every card number back.

gates.says: all 12 of this quiz's discriminating readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-deposit-in-chip-data:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-deposit-in-chip-data:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-deposit-in-chip-data:a: 14.1 shows the 'tip written into field 4 and 9F02' case failing the issuer's recomputation, so making the two amounts agree does not get the purchase approved.
recorded.prompt:q-deposit-in-chip-data:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-deposit-in-chip-data:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-deposit-in-chip-data:c: 14.1 says the issuer finds each covered value by its tag, so their order in DE 55 doesn't matter, and only the new 9F02 value broke the match.
recorded.prompt:q-deposit-in-chip-data:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-deposit-in-chip-data:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-deposit-in-chip-data:d: 14.1 says the cryptogram covers the amount, currency, date, type, the terminal's random number, the counter and more, not just the card number and counter.
recorded.prompt:q-gateway-field-list:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-gateway-field-list:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-gateway-field-list:b: 14.2 says the liability split applies 'whatever the amount', so no amount threshold applies.
recorded.prompt:q-gateway-field-list:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-gateway-field-list:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-gateway-field-list:c: 14.2 says the customer did authenticate, but outside the authorization, and the authorization is all the issuer gets.
recorded.prompt:q-gateway-field-list:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-gateway-field-list:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-gateway-field-list:d: 14.2 says what decides liability is whether the result reached the issuer in the authorization; the page never mentions the directory server reporting results, so it refutes this option only indirectly.
recorded.prompt:q-token-without-range:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-token-without-range:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-token-without-range:b: 14.3 says a token with no reserved BIN is routed to the issuer of whatever range it falls in, and only a reserved range lets a system see that it holds a token.
recorded.prompt:q-token-without-range:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-token-without-range:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-token-without-range:c: 14.3 and 14.9 say a token passes the Luhn check, and that length and check digit can't tell a token from a card number.
recorded.prompt:q-token-without-range:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-token-without-range:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-token-without-range:d: 14.3 says the token reaches the issuer of its range as a card number, and its note says vault tokens are turned back into card numbers before anything goes to the network, so issuers never consult the vault.
recorded.prompt:q-shop-app-detokenize:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-shop-app-detokenize:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-shop-app-detokenize:b: 14.3 says random tokens carry nothing of the card, so a leaked token table is only a list of numbers and the vault holds the only map back.
recorded.prompt:q-shop-app-detokenize:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-shop-app-detokenize:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-shop-app-detokenize:c: Partly true per the page: 14.4 says tokens are issued per requestor, so a leaked token doesn't pay at another shop, but 14.5's detokenize permission turns them into card numbers that work anywhere.
recorded.prompt:q-shop-app-detokenize:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-shop-app-detokenize:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-shop-app-detokenize:d: 14.5 ties the right to the app's own credentials and says a thief in the app can use it; the page never mentions a network-location restriction.

gates.says: each of the 4 questions keys exactly 1 of its distinct options and every option carries the sentence its reader is shown
each of the 4 questions cites a passage the ledger still digests to the value this exercise was built from
